careers.name: Software Engineer
careers.description: Design, build, and maintain software applications and systems.
careers.aiExposureRationale: Software development is entirely digital work focused on coding, architecture, and algorithm design—core domains where LLMs are achieving human-level proficiency. Large Language Models can now write functional code, debug programs, and generate documentation at scale, significantly increasing individual productivity and potentially reducing headcount despite strong demand.

careers.name: Doctor (General Practitioner)
careers.description: Diagnose and treat illnesses, provide preventive care, and manage patient health.
careers.aiExposureRationale: Medicine involves a significant amount of digital knowledge work, including diagnosis through image analysis and treatment planning, where AI is rapidly advancing. However, the core requirement for physical patient examination, real-time clinical judgment in emergencies, surgical intervention, and the legal/ethical accountability of a medical license creates a strong barrier to full automation despite major productivity gains in diagnostic and administrative tasks.

careers.name: Investment Banker
careers.description: Advise corporations on mergers, acquisitions, and capital raising.
careers.aiExposureRationale: The core work involves analyzing market data, researching investments, and generating reports—all digital tasks where AI excels. While client relationships and complex advisory roles provide some insulation, algorithmic trading, robo-advisors, and AI-driven portfolio management are already reducing the need for human intermediaries in securities sales.

careers.name: Mechanical Engineer
careers.description: Design and develop mechanical systems, from engines to robotics.
careers.aiExposureRationale: The core work of designing mechanical systems, performing simulations, and drafting technical specifications is increasingly performed using digital CAD and simulation software that is highly susceptible to AI-driven optimization and automation. While physical prototyping and manufacturing oversight provide a buffer, the heavy reliance on computer-aided design and complex data analysis makes the occupation highly exposed to AI-driven productivity gains and task automation.
pros: Tangible impact — you build real things

careers.name: Lawyer
careers.description: Represent clients in legal matters, draft contracts, and argue cases in court.
careers.aiExposureRationale: The core tasks of legal research, document review, and contract drafting are fundamentally digital and highly susceptible to AI automation. While the role requires high-level strategic judgment, court appearances, and client relationship management, LLMs are already proficient at analyzing case law and generating legal memoranda, significantly increasing productivity and reducing routine legal work.

careers.name: Clinical Psychologist
careers.description: Assess, diagnose, and treat mental health conditions through therapy and research.
careers.aiExposureRationale: While AI can significantly assist with routine cognitive-behavioral interventions and preliminary mental health screening through chatbots, the core of clinical psychology requires deep empathy, real-time therapeutic presence, and complex interpersonal judgment in crisis situations that AI cannot replicate. The role's requirement for licensed clinical assessment and ethical accountability provides substantial protection against full automation.
cons: Can be lower pay vs. other doctoral professions

careers.name: Management Consultant
careers.description: Advise organisations on strategy, operations, and organisational improvement.
careers.aiExposureRationale: Management analysts perform work that is almost entirely digital, involving data analysis, process mapping, and the generation of strategic recommendations. AI is highly capable of automating the core tasks of this role, including identifying operational inefficiencies, benchmarking against industry standards, and drafting improvement proposals, though human judgment remains necessary for complex stakeholder negotiations and implementation oversight.

careers.name: Architect
careers.description: Design buildings and spaces that are functional, safe, and aesthetically compelling.
careers.aiExposureRationale: Architects perform high-level knowledge work that is increasingly digital, utilizing CADD and BIM software which is highly susceptible to AI-driven automation in generative design and technical documentation. While the role requires physical site visits and complex client negotiations, a significant portion of the core work—drafting, specification writing, and regulatory compliance—is moving toward high AI integration.

careers.name: Diplomat
careers.description: Represent a country's interests abroad, negotiate treaties, and manage international relations.
careers.aiExposureRationale: Diplomacy requires in-person negotiation, cultural sensitivity, crisis management, and real-time relationship-building across governments that AI cannot replicate. While AI enhances translation, intelligence analysis, and communication drafting, the core work of building trust, reading political dynamics, and representing sovereign interests in high-stakes settings remains fundamentally human.

careers.name: Environmental Scientist
careers.description: Research and advise on environmental issues including pollution, conservation, and climate change.
careers.aiExposureRationale: This occupation involves a significant amount of digital knowledge work, including data analysis, report writing, and regulatory compliance, which are highly susceptible to AI augmentation. However, the role is anchored by a physical component involving fieldwork, site inspections, and laboratory sample analysis that AI cannot currently replicate. AI will likely serve as a powerful tool for modeling environmental impacts and drafting technical documents, increasing individual productivity while leaving the physical data collection and stakeholder relationship management to humans.
pros: Growing field due to climate focus
cons: Lower pay compared to other sciences

careers.name: Film Director / Producer
careers.description: Lead creative vision for film and media projects, managing teams and production.
careers.aiExposureRationale: The core work involves high-level creative decision-making and real-time on-set management, which remain fundamentally human functions. However, the occupation is increasingly exposed as AI advances in script analysis, automated editing, visual effects generation, and casting recommendations, significantly augmenting creative workflows and potentially reducing the number of decision-makers needed for large-scale productions.

careers.name: Product Manager
careers.description: Define product strategy, prioritise features, and coordinate engineering and design teams.
careers.aiExposureRationale: Product management is heavily digital, involving requirements writing, data analysis, competitive research, and stakeholder communication—all areas where AI is rapidly advancing. AI can automate roadmap generation, user research synthesis, and feature prioritization frameworks. However, the role requires cross-functional leadership, navigating organizational ambiguity, and building alignment across teams through interpersonal influence that remains fundamentally human.

careers.name: Data Analyst
careers.description: Collect, process, and analyse data to help organisations make informed decisions.
careers.aiExposureRationale: Data science is a fully digital occupation centered on coding, statistical modeling, and data analysis—all areas where AI is rapidly achieving parity or superiority. While human judgment is still needed for business context and ethical oversight, AI can now automate significant portions of the data pipeline, including cleaning raw data, generating complex code, and even suggesting optimal model architectures.
pros: Clear career progression to data science

careers.name: Accountant
careers.description: Prepare and examine financial records, ensure compliance, and advise on tax strategy.
careers.aiExposureRationale: Accountancy is a fundamentally digital occupation centered on data analysis, regulatory compliance, and reporting, all of which are highly susceptible to AI and robotic process automation. While high-level advisory roles and complex forensic audits require human judgment and relationship management, the core tasks of data organization, tax computation, and anomaly detection are increasingly being automated, significantly increasing worker productivity and restructuring the entry-level labor market.

careers.name: Secondary School Teacher
careers.description: Teach specialist subjects to students aged 11-18 in secondary schools.
careers.aiExposureRationale: While AI can significantly automate lesson planning, grading, and content delivery through personalized tutoring systems, the core of this occupation involves real-time classroom management, student motivation, and complex interpersonal interactions that require human presence. Teaching remains fundamentally grounded in the physical classroom and the human relationships essential to adolescent development.

careers.name: Primary School Teacher
careers.description: Teach core subjects and support holistic development of children aged 4-11.
careers.aiExposureRationale: The core of teaching involves real-time human interaction, classroom management, and the emotional support of children, which AI cannot replicate. While AI can significantly assist with peripheral tasks like lesson planning, grading, and generating individualized learning recommendations, the fundamental requirement for physical presence, real-time behavioral intervention, and the development of meaningful relationships between teacher and student provides a strong barrier to automation.

careers.name: HR Professional
careers.description: Manage recruitment, employee relations, training, and workplace policy.
careers.aiExposureRationale: Human resources is a predominantly digital and data-driven occupation involving recruitment, performance analysis, and compliance documentation that are highly susceptible to AI automation. While the role requires interpersonal skills and complex conflict resolution, AI can automate significant portions of candidate screening, benefits administration, and policy compliance monitoring, leading to major restructuring and productivity gains.
cons: Can be caught between management and staff

careers.name: Marketing & PR Professional
careers.description: Develop campaigns, manage brand reputation, and communicate with target audiences.
careers.aiExposureRationale: PR specialists perform predominantly digital work involving content creation, data analysis, and social media strategy—all areas where AI is rapidly advancing. While high-level client relationships and crisis communication require human judgment, the core tasks of drafting press releases, monitoring media coverage, and analyzing audience metrics are highly susceptible to AI-driven automation.
cons: Can be high-pressure with tight deadlines
Agency culture can mean long hours

careers.name: Graphic & Multimedia Designer
careers.description: Create visual content for print, digital, and interactive media using design software.
careers.aiExposureRationale: Graphic design is a fully digital occupation centered on creating visual content using software tools—a domain where generative AI is rapidly advancing. AI can now generate layouts, color schemes, and even complete designs from text prompts, significantly increasing productivity and potentially reducing the number of human designers needed for routine commercial work.
pros: Portfolio-based — your work speaks for itself
cons: Can be lower pay early on

careers.name: Journalist / Writer
careers.description: Research, write, and publish stories for newspapers, magazines, websites, or broadcast media.
careers.aiExposureRationale: Journalism is experiencing severe disruption as AI can now generate news summaries, conduct automated fact-checking, and produce basic news articles from raw data feeds. While investigative reporting and on-scene presence provide some protection, the BLS projects significant decline due to AI's ability to research, write, and distribute news content at scale.

careers.name: Police Officer
careers.description: Maintain public safety, investigate crimes, and enforce the law within communities.
careers.aiExposureRationale: The occupation is a hybrid of physical patrol and digital detective work. While AI can significantly automate crime analysis, facial recognition, and report writing, the core duties of physical law enforcement, crisis intervention, and real-time community presence require human judgment and physical capability that AI cannot replicate.

careers.name: Social Worker
careers.description: Support vulnerable individuals and families, safeguard children, and connect people with services.
careers.aiExposureRationale: Social work requires physical presence, deep cultural competence, and real-time human judgment in emotionally complex situations that AI cannot replicate. While AI can assist with peripheral administrative tasks like case documentation and resource matching, the core work of building trust with vulnerable populations and providing crisis intervention remains fundamentally human-centric.

careers.name: Civil Engineer
careers.description: Design and oversee construction of infrastructure — roads, bridges, buildings, and water systems.
careers.aiExposureRationale: Civil engineering involves significant digital knowledge work, including CAD design, data analysis, and cost estimation, which are highly susceptible to AI-driven productivity gains. However, the role is anchored by the necessity for physical site inspections, real-world surveying, and the legal accountability of a Professional Engineer (PE) license, which requires human judgment and liability that AI cannot currently replace.

careers.name: Actuary
careers.description: Use mathematics, statistics, and financial theory to assess risk for insurance and pensions.
careers.aiExposureRationale: Actuarial work is fundamentally digital, involving the analysis of large datasets, statistical modeling, and financial forecasting—all areas where AI and machine learning excel. While the profession requires high-level human judgment and the ability to explain complex risks to stakeholders, the core technical tasks of data compilation and probability estimation are highly susceptible to automation and significant productivity gains through AI.

careers.name: Cyber Security Professional
careers.description: Protect organisations from cyber threats by designing, monitoring, and responding to security incidents.
careers.aiExposureRationale: Information security analysis is a digital-first occupation centered on monitoring networks, identifying vulnerabilities, and responding to cyber threats—all areas where AI is rapidly advancing. AI can automate threat detection, vulnerability scanning, and incident response, significantly increasing analyst productivity. However, high-level strategic decision-making and complex incident investigation provide some insulation from full automation.

careers.name: Biologist / Lab Scientist
careers.description: Conduct research in genetics, microbiology, ecology, or biomedical science in labs and the field.
careers.aiExposureRationale: The role is a hybrid of physical laboratory work and digital data analysis. While AI can significantly automate data interpretation, report writing, and experimental modeling, the core duties involve manual tasks like setting up equipment, preparing biological samples, and conducting physical experiments that require a human presence in a lab or field environment.

careers.name: Physiotherapist
careers.description: Help patients recover movement and manage pain through exercise, manual therapy, and education.
careers.aiExposureRationale: The core of physical therapy is highly hands-on, requiring manual dexterity for patient treatment, real-time assessment of movement and pain, and direct clinical intervention that AI cannot replicate. While AI will significantly enhance diagnostic accuracy through motion analysis and assist with peripheral administrative and planning tasks, the fundamental requirement for human presence and tactile therapeutic work creates a strong barrier to high exposure.
pros: Can work privately or in NHS/hospitals

careers.name: Events Manager
careers.description: Plan, coordinate, and deliver events from conferences to festivals and corporate functions.
careers.aiExposureRationale: Event planning involves significant digital knowledge work, such as budgeting, vendor coordination via email, and logistics scheduling, all of which are highly susceptible to AI automation. However, the role requires substantial physical presence for on-site setup and real-time problem-solving during events, as well as high-touch interpersonal relationship management with clients and vendors that AI cannot currently replicate.

careers.name: Quantity Surveyor
careers.description: Manage costs on construction projects from initial estimates through to final accounts.
careers.aiExposureRationale: Surveying is a hybrid occupation involving physical fieldwork with specialized equipment alongside digital data processing and legal documentation. While drone technology and AI-powered analysis of geospatial data significantly enhance productivity, the requirement for legal licensure, physical site validation, and professional liability means human surveyors remain essential for certification and final verification.
